memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "His brothers then came and threw themselves down before him. 'We are your slaves,' they said." — Gen 50:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now they come in person, and they throw themselves down. "We are your slaves."

They are offering the only thing they can think of — themselves, in servitude — because they still believe the debt must be paid somehow. If Joseph will not take revenge, then perhaps he will take their freedom.

And notice, once more, that Joseph's boyhood dreams have come true. The sheaves bowing, the sun and moon and stars bowing (Gen 37:5-11). The very dreams that made them hate him enough to sell him.

But look at what Joseph does with the fulfilment. Nothing. He does not use it. He has no interest in being their master.

That is worth sitting with. Some people spend their lives waiting for the moment they can say "I was right" to those who wronged them. Joseph has that moment handed to him, twice over, and he refuses it entirely.

Being vindicated is not the same as needing to make someone pay. Paul wrote that love keeps no record of wrongs (1 Cor 13:5).

And God does not want your servitude either. He is not looking for slaves working off a debt. Jesus said, "I no longer call you servants... I have called you friends" (Jn 15:15).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you waiting for a chance to prove you were right?
2. Do you relate to God as a slave working off a debt, or as a friend?
3. What would you do if vindication were handed to you tomorrow?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, take from me the desire to make anyone pay. Thank You that You do not want me as a slave working off a debt, but as Your child and friend. Amen.
